newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade slow at $67,dn $1-trade.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade slow at $67,dn $1-trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Thursday quietly slipped to $67.00 per cwt in light volume, down $1.00 from this week's active sales and down $2.00 from the bulk of trade last week, feedlot sources said.
About 2,200 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, which brought week-to-date sales near 91,000 head. Most showlists were nearly sold out, sources there said.
In Kansas, about 1,300 head sold, which brought the week-to-date movement near 75,000. Most market-ready cattle were sold from showlists there as well, Kansas cattle feeders said.
There likely will be some carryover into next week of cattle not sold in Kansas this week but many of those were "green" or unfinished, a Kansas feedyard manager said.
Packers lowered bids to $67.00 from $68.00 sales this week when beef prices tumbled Wednesday and again Thursday under the weight of large cattle slaughter, sources said.
USDA Thursday estimated week-to-date cattle slaughter at 529,000 head, above 516,000 in the same period a week ago and 528,000 a year ago.
Beef cut-out prices Thursday were quoted down $0.65 to $1.16 per cwt, on 324 fabricated loads sold, USDA said. Heavyweight choice beef prices fell $0.65 to $105.20, a drop of $1.48 since Tuesday.
But reported beef sales for the week to date totaled 1,089 fabricated loads, compared with 777 last week, according to USDA statistics.
